title: Which integers lie between two numbers?
description: Four pairs of numbers sit on the number line, the smaller number on the left. Every integer strictly between the two numbers of a pair is written from left to right, so the two ends are left out and zero is written when it lies inside. The video breaks the slip of reading minus fifteen as bigger than minus eight.
teaching_notes: One idea: put the smaller number on the left of the number line, then list the integers strictly between the two. Watch for students who include the two ends, or who think minus fifteen is bigger than minus eight.

video_script.why: The child lists the integers between two numbers by reading the number line from left to right.
video_script.substitution: The book's four pairs of numbers, each placed on the number line of the chapter.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book, with zero in the middle and negative numbers to its left
video_script.payoff_line: Every list runs from smallest to largest and leaves out the two ends

final_answer.spoken: minus six to minus one, minus three to three, minus fourteen to minus nine, and minus twenty nine to minus twenty four

never_show: the two ends of a pair inside its list
maths_rules: −7 < 0, so −7 is on the left; the integers between are −6, −5, −4, −3, −2, −1 (6 of them)
−4 < 4, so −4 is on the left; the integers between are −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 (7 of them)
−15 < −8, so −15 is on the left; the integers between are −14, −13, −12, −11, −10, −9 (6 of them)
−30 < −23, so −30 is on the left; the integers between are −29, −28, −27, −26, −25, −24 (6 of them)
check: from −30 to −23 is 7 steps, so 7 − 1 = 6 integers lie between
